reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 08, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png; checked the near-profile pose, cap, visible profile-side brow and covered hair, absence of facial hair and glasses, one mouth, uniform/ribbon/pendant, crop, lighting, collar fit, complete card/note/backplate and visible transparency.

entries.positive_observation: The light gray/olive peaked cap with darker band, small pale-gold front insignia and dark visor remains, with hair mostly covered and the visible light brown-gray profile-side eyebrow retained. The chin is smooth with no moustache or beard, there is one stern closed mouth, and no spectacles were added. The strong three-quarter to near-profile head facing viewer left and matching gaze are preserved rather than rotated frontal; three-quarter shoulders, chest-up crop, warm directional facial light and visor shadow remain. The olive-gray uniform keeps light patterned collar patches, one visible gold-toned shoulder edge, one pale/red neck ribbon and one small silver-toned pendant. The collar sits coherently around a short broad neck below the rounded chin without a stalk, pinching, clipping or cream bib. The complete tilted dark frame, opaque light muted photographic backplate, overlapping warm-cream note with compact upper marks and mostly blank lower paper, and small dark right-edge tab remain. Full white/cyan inspection shows a genuine transparent exterior without visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte halo.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept native RGBA extrema 0..254 following actual white/cyan/alpha inspection; no source-alpha replacement was performed or needed, and near-opacity values alone were not rejection grounds.
entries.visible_limitations: Only the profile-side brow and hair edge are visible, and tiny cap, collar and pendant details cannot be read exactly at 65x67; no hidden-side feature or exact emblem is claimed. Note marks remain indistinct visual groups rather than readable text.
